name: french_01
context: A French tweet from the DEFT 2017 dataset, posted between 2014 and 2016. The dataset was built to study opinion and figurative language, so it includes ironic, sarcastic and humorous tweets. Annotators labelled the overall polarity of each tweet.

versions.analysis_for_next:
Version 0 told the model to judge the polarity of the reported content. This made it over-polarize: neutral recall was only 82/197. 63 neutral texts went to positive and 52 to negative.

Neutral texts predicted positive are mostly factual news about renewable energy, innovations, investments and projects:
- 'tuiles transparentes pour capter l'énergie solaire'
- '519 millions $ ... centrale solaire'
- 'l'hydroélectricité est en plein essor'
- 'cabines téléphoniques ... écologiques'

Neutral texts predicted negative are factual headlines about bad events with no added author judgement:
- 'La fonte des calottes polaires s'accélère'
- 'pourrait causer 250.000 décès'
- 'Des arbres coupés...'
- 'Polémique autour...'
- 'péage poids lourd suspendu'

They also include sarcastic jokes and banter that annotators kept neutral ('Je leur donne le sein, c'est plus écologique', 'servent à faire du vent').

So these annotators label news headlines neutral unless the tweeter adds an evaluation: an exclamation, '#goodnews', 'Incroyable', 'Bravo', insults, or a clear opinion. The topic's good or bad nature does not decide the label on its own.

Positive-gold errors predicted neutral (e.g. 'Les banques s'invitent dans l'écosystème du crowdfunding', 'Comprendre la géothermie') look noisy, and I will not chase them. Positive-gold errors predicted negative are often opinionated tweets where the author supports a cause by criticising its opposite ('fausse solution gaz de schiste', 'il est grand temps d'agir', 'mieux vaut des avions que vos éoliennes'). Here the author is advocating, and annotators read that as positive.

Negative recall is high (181/200), so I can afford to push dry bad-news headlines toward neutral.

Plan for the new version:
- Make neutral the default for third-person headlines.
- Require an explicit author stance for positive or negative.
- Treat advocacy for solutions as positive.
- Treat light jokes as neutral.

Version 1 collapsed to 50.2 macro-F1. Telling the model to ignore the reported content and look only for author stance sent 113 positive and 80 negative texts to neutral.

The errors show these annotators do label headline content. Bare headlines are positive when they report progress: 'cellule solaire qui stocke', 'éoliennes installées avec succès', 'centrale hydroélectrique', 'aides renforcées', 'lancent un projet pilote'. They are negative when they report harm: 'manchot empereur victime', 'suspension de l'écotaxe', 'enfer climatique', 'espèces invasives menacent', 'scandale'. So version 0's content-polarity approach (64.9) was right, and I return to it.

The errors also confirm literal reading of irony: 'Bravo aux jeunes UDC...', 'la police stimule la croissance', 'prix pinocchio' and '#MerciSégolène' are all gold positive. Surface wording wins.

Version 0's main weakness was neutral recall. The neutral texts it got wrong are inconsistent with gold elsewhere (similar solar headlines are gold positive), so I will make only small, safe additions:
- Playful wordplay or puns on 'écologique', 'éolienne' or 'vent' with no real event are neutral.
- Personal anecdotes and descriptive explanations (how something works, what a term means, statistics) are neutral.
- Headlines that merely mention a topic or a debate without a clear good or bad outcome are neutral.

I keep the content-polarity rule for real outcomes.

Version 2 (content polarity with a literal reading of irony) reached 67.4, the best so far.

The largest remaining clean pattern is positive texts predicted neutral. These are tweets that offer learning or reading resources:
- 'Comprendre la géothermie'
- 'un peu d'histoire pour mieux comprendre'
- 'Devenez incollable sur les éoliennes'
- 'Instructif. A regarder'
- 'Pour les parisiens que ça intéresse'
- 'Nouveau Quizz'
- 'Guide méthodologique'
- 'Tour d'horizon'
- 'Portrait des usages et meilleures pratiques'

Annotators consistently mark explainers, guides, quizzes and recommendations positive. Business 'écosystème' growth stories ('Les banques s'invitent dans l'écosystème du crowdfunding') are also positive. I will move these into positive and out of the neutral description.

Neutral texts predicted positive are mostly green-tech headlines, and gold is inconsistent on them. I will add only a mild rule: speculative forecasts or questions ('pourrait devenir', 'en 2035 ?') and plain descriptions of a building or object with no achievement are neutral.

Neutral texts predicted negative (dramatic news) are inconsistent with the negative gold, so I leave them alone. Everything else stays to protect what works.

Version 3 fell to 66.4 from 67.4. The new rule calling explainers, quizzes and resources positive fixed a few positives (positive recall 142, up from 137) but pulled more neutral texts into positive (68, up from 59):
- 'Nouveau Quizz ... Fruits et légumes'
- 'Notice bibliographique'
- 'schéma explicatif'
- 'Connaître et maîtriser les outils'
- 'Tour d'horizon'
- 'Présentation du Porte-queue'

So resource-sharing is inconsistent in gold, and I remove that rule.

The persistent problem is still neutral texts predicted positive. They are green-tech or project headlines that describe what a thing is or does, give a sum of money, or forecast something ('tuiles transparentes pour capter', 'maisons écologiques', 'pourrait devenir', 'va être testé', '185 millions pour'). The positive-gold headlines lean more on explicit achievement or approval words ('installées avec succès', 'aides renforcées', 'salue', 'lauréat', 'à l'honneur', 'applaudissent', 'rassure').

For version 4 I return to version 2 and sharpen this distinction gently. A headline that merely presents a technology, building, sum or plan without an achievement or approval word leans neutral. One with success, approval, award, reinforcement or celebration is positive. I keep the literal reading of irony and the negative handling, which work well (negative recall 174–176).

Version 4 reached 68.6, the best so far, but it over-corrected. Positive recall dropped to 112, with 67 positive texts predicted neutral. Neutral recall rose to 126, with only 30 neutral texts predicted positive.

Many of the positive texts lost to neutral are headlines where an actor concretely carries out or decides a green action:
- 'Sunzil et Ingeteam lancent un projet pilote'
- 'inauguration de la plateforme'
- 'Technip lance un investissement majeur'
- 'Genève mise sur la géothermie'
- 'L'Assemblée vote la réduction du nucléaire'
- 'Un champ de 17 300 panneaux bientôt opérationnel'
- 'Les Belges vont pouvoir construire la plus grande ferme éolienne'
- 'rues éclairées par l'énergie solaire'
- 'Déploiement du projet'
- 'remet en service'
- '40 milliards à mobiliser pour promouvoir'

The neutral texts that remain predicted positive are mostly descriptive, promotional or rhetorical: '... au coeur de la révolution', 'à la pointe', 'L'option la plus économique', 'Best-of', slogans, political rally lines.

Plan for version 5:
- Treat an actor launching, inaugurating, building, deploying, voting, investing in, backing or betting on a green project as positive.
- Keep neutral for descriptions of what a technology is or does, pure statistics, forecasts and tests, and generic slogans or catchphrases.
- Leave negative unchanged; it stays strong at about 177/200.

Version 5 (67.2) did slightly worse than version 4 (68.6). Adding action verbs ('lance', 'investissement') as positive cues did not recover positives. Instead it sent several neutral texts to positive ('NASA lance', 'L'investissement ... a atteint 8 milliards', '20 millions d'euros pour') and dropped positive recall to 109. The differences between versions are near the noise level, and gold is inconsistent on bare green-tech headlines.

The positive-gold texts still predicted neutral share a clearer signal: the headline frames an innovation or idea as a benefit, solution or improvement. Examples:
- 'Une étape prometteuse'
- 'moins bruyantes grâce au hibou'
- 'Une cellule solaire capable de stocker son énergie !'
- 'c'est possible'
- 'pour résoudre les problèmes'
- 'une solution locale'
- 'le solaire est l'énergie la moins chère'
- 'Vers une amélioration'
- 'ne plus subir, mais anticiper'
- 'écosystème unique d'une grande richesse'

The neutral-gold texts predicted positive are mostly sums of money, campaigns, forecasts, decrees, consultations, slogans and descriptions of objects or places.

The version 4 neutral example 'des tuiles transparentes pour capter l'énergie solaire' appears in gold as both neutral and positive. It probably taught the model to neutralise all innovations, so I replace it with the planned-test and funding-amount examples.

For version 6 I start from version 4 and make three changes:
- Positive now covers improvements, solutions, benefits or advantages (prometteuse, grâce à, capable de, moins cher, solution, possible, amélioration), plus achievements and approvals.
- Neutral now covers sums of money, planned tests, forecasts, decrees or consultations, slogans, and plain descriptions of a place or object.
- Generic action verbs ('lance', 'investissement') are removed from the positive cues.

Negative stays unchanged.

versions.analysis_for_next:
Scores have plateaued: version 2 got 67.4, version 4 68.6, version 5 67.2 and version 6 67.6. The remaining errors are largely annotation inconsistency.

The gold is inconsistent in three places:
- Near-identical green-tech headlines are labelled both neutral and positive ('tuiles transparentes', 'cellule solaire qui stocke').
- Dramatic bad-news headlines are split between neutral and negative ('fonte des calottes' is neutral, 'manchot empereur victime' is negative).
- Some anti-ecology complaints are gold positive.

Version 4 had the best balance. Neutral recall was 126 with a bare-description neutral example, and negative held at 177.

Version 6 recovered a few positives with improvement-framing cues ('prometteuse', 'grâce à', 'capable de') but lost neutral by replacing the tuiles example. Version 5's generic action verbs ('lance', 'investissement') pulled neutral funding and campaign headlines into positive.

For version 7 I keep version 4 nearly intact, including its neutral examples. I add only the narrow positive framing cues that signal a benefit or improvement ('prometteuse', 'grâce à', 'moins cher', 'solution', 'inauguration', 'mise sur'). I do not add generic action verbs or sums of money. The not_for fields state the boundary explicitly: an explicit benefit or improvement word makes a headline positive, while a bare 'X pour faire Y' description stays neutral.

Version 7 is the best so far at 69.2. Its confusion matrix shows that negative is solid (179/200) and neutral recall is the highest yet (127/197). Positive recall is still the weak point: 113/203, with 64 positive texts going to neutral.

Many of those 64 are headlines about a green capacity being expanded or brought into service:
- 'accroitre la production d'énergie solaire'
- 'la plus grande ferme éolienne'
- 'bientôt opérationnel'
- 'Déploiement du projet'
- 'rues éclairées par l'énergie solaire'
- 'usine ... autorisée pour produire du gaz vert'
- 'Assemblée vote la réduction du nucléaire'

Version 5 showed that generic verbs ('lance', 'investissement', money amounts) pull neutral funding and campaign headlines into positive. So I will add only expansion and coming-into-service wording, not generic launch or money words:
- accroître (increase)
- plus grand (largest)
- bientôt opérationnel (soon operational)
- déploiement (deployment)
- autorisée (authorised)
- vote la réduction (votes to reduce)

The rest of version 7 stays unchanged, including the neutral examples (tuiles, test, Ademe, vent pun) that anchor neutral recall. Gold is inconsistent on the remaining neutral-to-negative errors (dramatic news headlines) and on the positive-to-negative ones (complaints written from a pro-ecology stance), so I leave both alone.

Version 8 scored 69.2, the same as version 7, with almost the same confusion matrix. Adding the expansion cues moved only about 2 texts.

One untested pattern remains in the positive texts predicted neutral. Announcements of events, launches, forums, summits, workshops, festivals and talks that promote a sustainable or energy theme are labelled positive by these annotators:
- 'Lancement européen de la MOVE Week'
- 'Les Journées de l'Industrie électrique ... dans 60 sites'
- 'Worshop sur le bruit des éoliennes'
- 'World Investment Forum ... Investir dans le développement durable'
- 'l'Inde s'apprête à accueillir le 1er Sommet Mondial des Investisseurs'
- 'Ouverture ... des travaux de l'atelier'
- 'Intervention sur Les TIC au service de l'environnement'
- 'Fête de la terre'
- 'Lancement de l'offre'

I see few neutral-gold texts of this kind. The neutral agenda texts are mostly personal meetings or TV schedules ('En réunion avec...', 'sera l'invitée', 'À 20h40 #lamaisonf5').

For version 9 I keep version 8 and add one change: launches and public events promoting green, energy or sustainable themes count as positive. Personal meetings, TV schedules and publications of figures stay neutral. The neutral meeting example ('En réunion avec ...') makes that boundary explicit.

Version 9 dropped to 68.1. Calling green-themed events and launches positive gained 15 positives but pulled 19 neutral texts into positive. Gold labels most event announcements neutral:
- 'Festival du Livre ... écologiques'
- 'SAVE THE DATE colloque'
- 'Rencontre régionales carbone'
- 'table ronde'
- 'Atelier de copro'
- 'Business Forum'
- 'expositions'
- 'Cinema Green'
- 'journée de découverte'

The event rule was wrong, so I revert to version 8 (69.2, tied with version 7, the best). I also add the opposite clarification: event announcements are neutral unless they carry explicit success or benefit wording. In version 8 these texts were already mostly neutral, so this only reinforces what worked.

Everything else in version 8 stays:
- Content polarity for real outcomes.
- Ironic praise read literally.
- Bare technology, sum, forecast or test headlines are neutral.
- Expansion and benefit cues signal positive.
- Negative unchanged.
